stops.note: 'handwork', kheir 'hand' + ergon 'work'; the Hippocratic treatises On Fractures and On Joints set out surgical techniques
borrowed from Greek; Celsus's De Medicina (c. AD 30) devotes its last books to surgery
worn down from Old French cirurgie
Henry VIII's charter of 1540 united London's barbers and surgeons in one company; British doctors' 'surgery' hours come from the same word

current_meaning: the treatment of injuries or disease by cutting open the body
